subject: Temp key proxy & audit log routing — scope decision needed
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, compliance-team@medspring.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Temp key proxy & audit log routing — scope decision needed

Team,

Thanks for joining this thread. Medspring's security team emailed yesterday requesting a short-term path so they can keep customer-controlled keys for a 30-day diagnostic window while we deliver the longer BYOK integration. Two quick asks:

1) We need a recommended flow we can ship as an exception for the pilot (temporary proxy keys + segmented audit export).
2) Confirm what evidence (audit logs, timeline, token snapshots) we can produce from Hosted vs Dedicated without full BYOK.

I'm attaching a rough diagram of a possible proxy approach (temp-key-proxy-architecture.pdf) and the checklist Medspring wants.

Constraints to be mindful of: low-latency inference for their interactive product, no long-lived key material on our servers, and a clear audit trail that they can ingest into their SIEM.

Marissa — we need product clarity on acceptable UX and rollout guardrails (can this be opt-in per-project?).
Grace — security guidance on whether a short-lived key escrow/proxy plus segregated audit export satisfies SOC evidence requirements for an interim window.
Priyom — feasibility from infra: routing audit data to a customer-managed S3 endpoint vs sending packaged evidence.
Jonas — can you advise on support/resourcing for a one-off pilot runbook?

Medspring: can you confirm the minimum audit retention and whether a signed proof-of-rotation every 24h would be sufficient for compliance?

Thanks — Diego

--
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0189
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, compliance-team@medspring.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Temp key proxy & audit log routing — scope decision needed

+1 on the ask. A few product constraints and proposals:

- We can expose a per-project "temporary key proxy" toggle in the Console; enablement will create a short-lived proxy token (24-72h) scoped to the project's inference routes.
- UX caveat: developer will see a limited dashboard and a notice about the temporary nature — after the window ends, traffic falls back to Redwood-managed keys unless customer completes BYOK onboarding.
- Rollout: pilot-only feature flag; we should gate by "pilot approved" in the org profile to avoid accidental enablement.

Questions for Security/Infra: is 24-72h token rotation acceptable? Also, what logs do we need to surface in the console vs push to the customer's SIEM?

I'll draft a minimal UI flow and can demo early next week.

—Marissa
Product Manager — Security Integrations
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, compliance-team@medspring.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 12:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Temp key proxy & audit log routing — scope decision needed

Thanks — this looks workable as an interim model with caveats. High level:

- Short-lived proxy keys (<=72h) are acceptable if we guarantee ephemeral key material is never written to persistent storage unencrypted and rotation is auditable.
- Audit evidence: Medspring will need
  * request/response metadata (request id, model id, timestamps)
  * key rotation proofs (signed rotation events)
  * host-level delivery logs showing when and where an artifact was exported to their SIEM/S3
- For SOC evidence, a signed daily bundle (timestamped, signed by Redwood HSM) containing the rotation/transfer manifest should be acceptable for the 30-day window.

Risks: must ensure no fallback path that accidentally retains unrotated keys. We should scope the pilot to a single org and apply strict rate/feature caps.

Attaching a short checklist to cover evidence requirements and a sample signed-manifest format.

—Grace
Director, Security & Trust
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, compliance-team@medspring.com
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:09:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Temp key proxy & audit log routing — scope decision needed

Infra notes / feasibility:

- We can create a proxy service that mints ephemeral tokens via KMaaS and routes inference traffic with minimal change to the runtime. Estimated work: 2 sprints to build the proxy + 1 sprint to add signed-manifest export.
- Audit routing: two modes supported
  1) Push mode: Redwood pushes daily signed bundles to customer-provided S3 (preferred for pilot).
  2) Pull mode: Customer calls a secure API and pulls bundles (needs auth handshake).
- We must implement per-org sandboxing at the networking layer to ensure exported bundles are only accessible to Medspring.

Blockers / asks: clear product decision on rotation window (24h vs 72h) and whether we support push-only for pilot. Also need sign-off to allocate a small infra on-call for the pilot week.

—Priyom
Staff Infra Engineer
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, compliance-team@medspring.com
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 12:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Temp key proxy & audit log routing — scope decision needed

Short answer on resourcing: we can staff the pilot if product narrows requirements today. My recommendation:

- Rotation policy: 48h to balance developer UX and operational headroom.
- Pilot export mode: push-only to customer S3 (reduces auth complexity).
- Limit pilot to: 1 org, 3 projects, daily signed-manifest export, clear rollback plan.

If everyone agrees, I'll get a small on-call rotation and formal runbook drafted.

—Jonas
VP, Product Ops
From: Compliance Team <compliance-team@medspring.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Temp key proxy & audit log routing — scope decision needed

Diego / team,

Thanks for the thoughtful options. Medspring is comfortable with the proposed pilot constraints: 48h rotation, push-only daily signed manifests to our S3, and the pilot scoping you suggested. We also confirm that the signed daily bundle plus request/response metadata is sufficient for our audit window.

Next steps from our side: provide S3 endpoint details and a short IP allowlist. We will also need the sample signed-manifest format (Grace mentioned an example).

We'll aim to have S3 details by EOD Wednesday.

—Tanya Kapoor
Senior Compliance Manager, Medspring
